instructions: Calm, warm science-documentary narrator. Unhurried, with a sense of wonder, clear articulation, a brief pause between sentences.

lines.text: This is a chaotic attractor of a language model's feedback loop, as numerical experiments show it: nearly three hundred thousand states of the model, from five hundred trajectories, projected onto three coordinates of its internal state. Each color is the most probable next token.
The states lie on thin, folded sheets instead of filling the space. Its Lyapunov dimension, an estimate from how fast nearby states separate and converge, is about one and a quarter.
At every step, nearby states move apart by about a third. Because they stay in a bounded region, they must be folded back. That stretching and folding is what makes the text unpredictable.
And all of it is one small model, with half a billion parameters, whose most likely next words, is, there and existence, come back over and over, never quite the same way twice.
